O acento tônico: a sílaba que manda: Word stress: the syllable in charge
PASSO 1: Toda palavra russa com duas síl: STEP 1: Every Russian word with two or more syllables has one stronger syllable. It is longer, louder and clearer. This is called word stress. STEP 2: In books, stress is shown as a small mark over the strong vowel. In «мама» (MAH-mah), the strength is on the first «ма». Say it slowly: MAH-mah, with the force on «MAH». STEP 3: In «она» (ah-NAH), the strength is on the last syllable. Say: ah-NAH, with the force on «NAH». Notice that the place of the stress changes from one word to another. STEP 4: One-syllable words, like «как» (kahk) and «кто» (kto), are strong all the way through. There is nothing to choose. STEP 5: Russian stress has no fixed place and is almost never written. So whenever you learn a new word, listen to the audio and remember where the stress is. It decides how the vowels sound, and you will see that in session 3.
em português o acento também muda a pala: in English, stress can change a word too: «REcord» (a noun) and «reCORD» (a verb), «PERmit» and «perMIT». Russian works the same way, except that the stress is almost never written.

Hoje chegam as sete letras mais traiçoei: Today the seven trickiest letters arrive: the false friends. They look like letters of the English alphabet, but they have a different sound. «В» looks like a B, but sounds like V. «Н» looks like an H, but sounds like N. «Р» looks like a P, but sounds like R. «С» looks like a C, but sounds like S. «У» looks like a Y, but sounds like «oo». «Х» looks like an X, but it is a rough «kh» from the throat, like «ch» in Scottish «loch». And «Е» sounds like «ye». Golden rule: if a letter looks Latin, be suspicious and listen.

Vogais sem acento: o «о» soa «а» e o «е»: Unstressed vowels: «о» sounds like «а» and «е» sounds like «и»
PASSO 1: A vogal com acento é clara e lo: STEP 1: A stressed vowel is clear and long. An unstressed vowel is weak and short, and it changes its sound. This is called vowel reduction. STEP 2: Unstressed «о» sounds like «а». In «она» (ah-NAH), the first letter is «о», but you say «ah». In «Москва» (mahsk-VAH), you say «mah», not «moh». STEP 3: Stressed «о» stays «о». In «кот» (koht) and in «метро» (mee-TROH), the «о» carries the stress and sounds like «о». STEP 4: Unstressed «е» sounds almost like «и», a quick «ee». In «метро», the first syllable sounds like «mee». In «сестра» (sees-TRAH), it sounds like «sees». In «ресторан» (rees-tah-RAHN), it sounds like «rees». STEP 5: The respelling next to each word, in this course, already shows the real pronunciation. When it differs from the spelling, trust the respelling and the audio.
você já faz isso em português sem perceb: you already do this in English without noticing: the unstressed «a» in «banana» or «about» turns into a weak «uh». In Russian the same happens to the «о» and the «е» that are far from the stress.
metrô: o «е» soa «и», lê-se mitró: metro: the «е» sounds like «и», read mee-TROH
Sem acento, o «е» soa «и» e a força cai: Unstressed, the «е» sounds like «и» and the stress falls on «ро»: mee-TROH.
«е» soa «и» e o «о» do meio soa «а»: «е» sounds like «и» and the middle «о» sounds like «а»
Consoantes sonoras e surdas: o final da: Voiced and voiceless consonants: the end of the word changes
PASSO 1: Consoante sonora é aquela em qu: STEP 1: A voiced consonant is one where your throat vibrates. Put a hand on your throat and say «v»: you feel it vibrate. Now say «f»: it does not vibrate. «f» is the voiceless partner of «v». STEP 2: Russian has pairs like this: «в» and «ф», «б» and «п», «д» and «т», «г» and «к», «з» and «с», «ж» and «ш». The first of each pair is the voiced one. Today you already know the voiced «в» and the voiceless «к», «т» and «с». The others come in the next lesson. STEP 3: The end-of-word rule: at the end of a word, a voiced consonant loses its vibration and becomes its voiceless partner. That is why «Романов» (rah-MAH-nahf) ends with an «f» sound, although it is written with «в». STEP 4: The neighbour rule: a voiced consonant also becomes voiceless before a voiceless one. In «вкус» (fkoos), which means «taste», the «в» sounds like «f» because it comes before «к». STEP 5: The spelling does not change, only the sound. Always write the word the way it is spelled, and speak the way the audio speaks.
em português a diferença entre «v» e «f»: in English the difference between «v» and «f» changes the word: «van» and «fan». It does in Russian too. But at the end of a word that difference disappears and only the voiceless sound is pronounced.

Sem «é» no presente e prática: No «is» in the present, and practice
Esta é Moscou. Aqui está o metrô, e lá o: This is Moscow. Here is the metro, and over there the theatre. Here is the restaurant. Here are Anna, Max and Vera. Anton is over there. He is not here. Who is this? This is Vera. She is the mother. Here the juice, here the cake, here the cupcake. Is this a cake? No, this is not a cake, it is a cupcake. Great! Thank you, mom!

Isto é «торт» ou «кекс»? Responda em rus: Is this «торт» or «кекс»? Answer in Russian.
PASSO 1: Em português você precisa do ve: STEP 1: In English you need the verb «to be»: «this is the mother». In Russian, in the present tense, that verb does not appear. STEP 2: To point something out, use «это» (EH-tah), which means «this» or «this is». Then say just the name of the thing: «Это мама» (EH-tah MAH-mah), literally «this mom». STEP 3: With «он» (ohn) and «она» (ah-NAH) it is the same: «Он Антон» (ohn ahn-TOHN), «Она мама» (ah-NAH MAH-mah). There is no word between the subject and the rest. STEP 4: To negate, put «не» (nyeh) before the word: «Это не торт» (EH-tah nyeh tort), this is not a cake. The word «нет» is kept for the short answer: «Нет». STEP 5: To ask a question, keep the same sentence and raise your voice on the word you are asking about: «Это торт?». The word order does not change. STEP 6: There is a word «есть» (yest), which the dictionary translates as «to be». In everyday speech it does not go in these sentences. Do not say «Это есть мама».
